flags.text: The stem capitalizes BOTH and AND for emphasis. Suggested wording for Thomas to review (not applied): plain case, "Which ion is isoelectronic with Ar and carries a +2 charge?" Key unchanged.

The bank explanation names only K+ and S2- as the other 18-electron species and says they are "failing the +2 requirement", which the house rule bars. Sc3+ and Cl- also have 18 electrons; the picture shows all five at 18 so the charge decides. Coach view only; bank text untouched.

served.stem: Argon (Z = 18) has the noble-gas configuration [Ne] 3s² 3p⁶ with 18 electrons. Among the following common ions, identify the one that is BOTH isoelectronic with Ar AND carries a +2 charge.
served.bankWhy: Isoelectronic with Ar means 18 electrons. Ca has Z = 20 and protons = 20; Ca²⁺ has lost 2 electrons → 18 e⁻, matching Ar. K⁺ and S²⁻ are also 18-electron species but carry +1 and -2 charges respectively, failing the +2 requirement.

answer.line: Every choice holds 18 electrons, so all five match argon. Only Ca^2+ also carries a +2 charge.

steps: Count electrons as Z minus charge for every choice: Ca^2+ 20 - 2, Sc^3+ 21 - 3, Cl^- 17 + 1, S^2- 16 + 2, K^+ 19 - 1. All 18.
So isoelectronic does not decide it. All five match argon's 18.
Read the second condition: a +2 charge. Only Ca^2+ is both.

choices.note: Sc^3+ does have 18 electrons, so it matches argon. Its charge is +3, not +2.
Cl^- gains one electron to reach 18. Its charge is -1, not +2.
S^2- matches argon and carries a 2, which pulls. The sign is negative; the stem asks for +2.
K^+ loses one electron to reach 18. Its charge is +1, not +2.

student.lockIt: Electrons = Z minus charge. Isoelectronic means equal electrons, so check the charge separately.
